plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch bulk RNA-seq count matrix (12,000 gene symbols x 12 samples, Salmon gene-level counts) with an unpaired 6 lesional atopic-dermatitis vs 6 control design in skin. The research question has two parts — which genes change, and which hallmark pathways change — plus an explicit instruction to handle the shallow library (sample_01, ~4x below median depth) carefully.

The order follows that structure. T1S1 does QC and depth diagnostics first, because the shallow-sample decision must be made on evidence rather than asserted: library sizes, detected-gene counts, VST/rlog PCA, and sample-sample correlation determine whether sample_01 is merely shallow (in which case DESeq2's size factors and dispersion shrinkage absorb it, and it stays) or is also an expression outlier separating from its group on PC1/PC2 (in which case exclusion is justified). Median-of-ratios size factors handle a 4x depth difference by construction; the real risk is that shallowness inflates dispersion and shrinks detection at low counts, so the step also quantifies how many genes drop below the independent-filtering threshold with and without the sample.

T1S2 runs the primary DESeq2 Wald test on all 12 samples with a ~condition design, then re-runs it excluding sample_01 as a prespecified sensitivity analysis, and reports the concordance between the two gene lists. Running both, and reporting the overlap, is the honest way to answer 'handle it carefully' — it converts a judgement call into a measured stability statement instead of hiding it in a preprocessing choice. Six vs six is modest but adequate for a negative-binomial GLM on a strong inflammatory contrast; effect-size shrinkage (apeglm) is used for ranking so that low-count genes with wild fold changes do not dominate.

T1S3 takes the shrunken ranking into fgsea against the staged human MSigDB hallmark collection (50 sets, HGNC symbols — matching the gene-symbol row identifiers in counts.csv, so no ID conversion is needed). GSEA on the full ranked list is preferred to over-representation on a thresholded list because it uses all genes and does not depend on an arbitrary FDR cutoff, which matters at n=6 per group. The same enrichment is repeated on the sensitivity ranking so pathway calls inherit the same stability check. Hallmark is the collection the question asks for; the staged GO branches are available as an optional mechanistic annotation only.

Only ~12,000 gene symbols are present, which is roughly half a full human annotation — the matrix is already pre-filtered, so an aggressive low-count filter would compound that. The steps therefore use a light independent filter and let DESeq2's own independent filtering do the rest.
